questions.question: Points A and B have position vectors (6, 6, 2) and (6, 0, 7) relative to fixed origin O. Line l1 passes through A and B. Write down an equation for l1 in the form r = p + lambda q.
steps: Use the position vector of A as p: p = (6, 6, 2).
Direction vector q = AB = OB - OA = (6 - 6, 0 - 6, 7 - 2) = (0, -6, 5).

questions.question: Line l2 has equation r = (3, 1, 4) + mu(1, 5, 9). Show that l1 and l2 do not meet.
questions.answer: The x-component gives mu = 3, then the y-component gives lambda = -5/3 and the z-component gives lambda = 29/5; these disagree, so the lines do not meet.
steps: Write l1 as (6, 6 - 6lambda, 2 + 5lambda) and l2 as (3 + mu, 1 + 5mu, 4 + 9mu).
The two values of lambda differ, so no values satisfy all three equations and the lines do not meet.

questions.question: Point C is on l2 where mu = -1. Find the acute angle between AC and l2, in degrees to one decimal place.
questions.answer: C = (2, -4, -5), AC = (-4, -10, -7), cos theta = 117/sqrt(17655), so theta = 28.3 degrees.
steps: AC . d = -4 - 50 - 63 = -117, so the modulus of the scalar product is 117.
|AC| = sqrt(165) and |d| = sqrt(107), so cos theta = 117/sqrt(17655) = 0.8805.

questions.question: With respect to a fixed origin O, l1 is r = (2i + 8j + 10k) + lambda(-i + 2j + 3k) and l2 is r = (-4i - j + 2k) + mu(5i + 4j + 8k), where lambda and mu are scalar parameters. Prove that l1 and l2 are skew.
questions.answer: Directions are not parallel and the equations give lambda = -3/2, mu = 3/2, which fail the third component, so the lines do not meet: they are skew.
steps: Direction vectors (-1, 2, 3) and (5, 4, 8) are not parallel, since their components are not in a constant ratio.
From the first two equations: mu = 3/2 and lambda = -3/2.
Check the third: 10 + 3(-3/2) = 5.5, but 2 + 8(3/2) = 14, so it fails.
The lines are not parallel and do not meet, so they are skew.

questions.question: Relative to origin O, line l has equation r = (1, -10, -9) + lambda(4, 4, 2). Given that vector OA is a unit vector parallel to l, find OA.
questions.answer: OA = (2/3, 2/3, 1/3), or its negative (-2/3, -2/3, -1/3) since either direction is parallel to l.
steps: Direction vector d = (4, 4, 2) has modulus sqrt(16 + 16 + 4) = 6.
A unit vector parallel to l is d/6 = (2/3, 2/3, 1/3).
The negative of this is also a unit vector parallel to l.

questions.question: The point X lies on l and is the point on l that is closest to the origin. Find the coordinates of X.
steps: A general point on l is X = (1 + 4lambda, -10 + 4lambda, -9 + 2lambda).
The closest point is where OX is perpendicular to d = (4, 4, 2), so X . d = 0.

questions.topic: Area of Triangle Using Vector Product
questions.question: The points O, X and A form triangle OXA. Find the exact area of triangle OXA.
steps: OX = (7, -4, -6) from part (b) and OA = (2/3, 2/3, 1/3) from part (a).
Its magnitude is sqrt(64 + 361 + 484)/3 = sqrt(909)/3 = sqrt(101).
Using OA = -(2/3, 2/3, 1/3) gives the same area.

questions.question: Lines l1: r = (2, 3, -7) + lambda(1, 2, 2) and l2: r = (2, 3, -7) + mu(4, -1, 8) meet at point P. State the coordinates of P.
steps: Both lines pass through the point with position vector (2, 3, -7), at lambda = 0 and mu = 0.
Since the lines meet at P, P is this common point.

questions.question: The angle between lines l1 and l2 is theta. Find the value of cos theta, giving the answer as a fully simplified fraction.
steps: Direction vectors are d1 = (1, 2, 2) and d2 = (4, -1, 8).

questions.question: Point Q lies on l1 where lambda = 6. Point R lies on l2 such that triangle QPR is isosceles with PQ = PR. Find the exact area of triangle QPR.
steps: R = P + mu(4, -1, 8), so |PR| = 9|mu| = 18, giving mu = 2 or -2.
For mu = 2, PR = (8, -2, 16) and PQ . PR = 216, so cos(QPR) = 216/324 = 2/3; for mu = -2 the cosine is -2/3.

questions.question: Find the coordinates of the possible positions of point R, where R lies on l2 and triangle QPR is isosceles with PQ = PR.
steps: R = (2, 3, -7) + mu(4, -1, 8), since P is on l2 at mu = 0.

questions.question: Line l1 has equation r = (8, 1, -3) + mu(-5, 4, 3). Point A lies on l1 where mu = 1. Find the coordinates of A.
steps: Substitute mu = 1 into the equation of l1.

questions.question: Point P has position vector (1, 5, 2). Line l2 passes through P and is parallel to l1. Write down a vector equation for l2.
steps: A line parallel to l1 has the same direction vector (-5, 4, 3).
Use P as the point on l2.

questions.question: Find the exact value of the distance AP, giving your answer in the form k sqrt(2), where k is a constant to be found.
The acute angle between AP and l2 is theta. Find the value of cos theta.
steps: AP = (-2, 0, 2) and the direction of l2 is d = (-5, 4, 3).

questions.question: A point E lies on l2 with AP = PE. Find the area of triangle APE.
steps: The angle between AP and l2 has cos 4/5, so sin = 3/5; the angle APE is theta or 180 - theta, so its sine is also 3/5.

questions.question: Find the coordinates of the two possible positions of E, where E lies on l2 and AP = PE.
steps: A point on l2 is E = (1 - 5t, 5 + 4t, 2 + 3t), so PE = (-5t, 4t, 3t).

questions.question: Lines l1: r = (4, -3, 2) + lambda(3, -2, -1) and l2: r = (2, 0, -9) + mu(2, -1, -3) meet at point X. Find the position vector of X.
steps: Substitute into the first: 4 + 3lambda = 8 + 4lambda, so lambda = -4 and mu = -5.
Check the third: 2 + 4 = 6 and -9 + 15 = 6, which is consistent.

questions.question: Point P(10, -7, 0) lies on l1. Point Q lies on l2 and PQ is perpendicular to l2. Calculate the coordinates of Q.

Line l has equation r = (4, 2, -3) + lambda(-4, -3, 5). Point A has position vector (9, -3, 2). X is the point on l nearest to A. Find (i) the coordinates of X, and (ii) the shortest distance from A to l, in the form sqrt(d) with d an integer.
steps: Let X = (4 - 4lambda, 2 - 3lambda, -3 + 5lambda); AX must be perpendicular to d = (-4, -3, 5).
Solve (A - p) . d = lambda |d|^2: 20 = 50lambda, so lambda = 2/5.

questions.question: Point B is the image of A after reflection in l. Find the position vector of B.
steps: X is the midpoint of A and B, so OB = 2OX - OA.

questions.question: Figure 1 shows parallelogram ABCD with AB = 6i - 2j + 3k and BC = 2i + 5j + 8k. Find the size of angle ABC in degrees to 2 decimal places.
steps: Angle ABC lies between BA = -AB = (-6, 2, -3) and BC = (2, 5, 8).

questions.question: Find the area of parallelogram ABCD, giving your answer to one decimal place (AB = 6i - 2j + 3k, BC = 2i + 5j + 8k).
steps: Area of a parallelogram is |AB x BC|.
So the area is 62.3 to one decimal place.

questions.question: Triangle PQR has PQ = 2i - 3j + 4k and PR = 8i - 5j + 3k. Find RQ.
Triangle PQR has PQ = 2i - 3j + 4k and PR = 8i - 5j + 3k. Find the size of angle PQR, in degrees, to three significant figures.
steps: Angle PQR is at Q, between QP = (-2, 3, -4) and QR = (6, -2, -1).
Angle PQR = arccos(-0.406) = 113.95 degrees, which is 114 degrees to 3 s.f.

questions.question: Relative to fixed origin O, A has position vector 4i + 8j + k and B has position vector 5i + 6j + 3k. The straight line l passes through A and B. Find a vector equation for l.
steps: Use A as the point on the line: r = (4, 8, 1) + t(1, -2, 2).

questions.question: Point P has position vector 2i - 2j + k. Point C lies on l so that PC is perpendicular to l. Find the coordinates of C.
steps: A general point on l is C = (4 + t, 8 - 2t, 1 + 2t).

questions.question: Point P' is the reflection of P in line l. Find the coordinates of P'.
steps: C is the foot of the perpendicular from P, so C is the midpoint of P and P'.

questions.question: Hence find |PP'|, giving your answer as a simplified surd.
